startup_resources.scope: Finite startup-memory comparison only, separate from load/performance screening and production RAM acceptance.
startup_resources.measurement: Kernel VmHWM plus five post-initial-cache-reload, post-single-UDP-query idle VmRSS/smaps RSS/PSS samples (KiB); no sustained traffic or injected resource limits

decision.criterion: Candidate 10,000-record median kernel VmHWM minus main median must be <=256 KiB, as stored in the plan before runs.
decision.limitation: 256 KiB is the predeclared allowance for checking removal of the added startup peak; it is not a project/device RAM budget or an equivalence claim against C.

limitations: Uses same-source Oracle release build, not the differently stripped SDK package ELF; both are separately identified in build evidence.
Each process completed initial cache reload, answered one UDP query, then produced five idle samples; no sustained traffic, saturation, or injected memory limits.

VmHWM is the kernel peak; per-run idle RSS/PSS are medians of five samples, then summary medians span three runs. The result does not close CPU/latency performance or target-router resource acceptance.

exclusions: R1/R4 and full affected-family closure are recorded by the main report/functional receipt, not inferred from these four startup results.
The 256 KiB criterion checks the repaired added peak at 10,000 host records; it is not a device RAM budget, C equivalence, or load/CPU/latency qualification.
